title: Scoped Sign-off Playbook: Customer-managed HSM + Delegated Operator Roles
creator: Asha Verma
description: This playbook defines the product requirements, decision criteria, and concrete sign-off checklist for private deployments where customers bring their own KMS/HSM and require delegated operator roles. The document scopes security and compliance acceptance items across SAML/SOAP SSO integrations, fine-grained RBAC mappings, tamper-evident audit logging, key escrow/rotation plans, and HSM quorum fallback. The goal is to create a repeatable, evidence-driven process that teams can execute during customer onboarding, security reviews, and release gating.
background: Several enterprise customers require customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed key material and want operators (Redwood or customer) to perform limited maintenance without creating a forensic audit gap. Past onboarding runs highlighted unclear expectations around operator key access, SAML assertion validation, and how audit chains are preserved across operator actions. This ticket consolidates those requirements into a single acceptance playbook and defines the artifacts required for sign-off.
scope:
- Requirements and acceptance criteria for SSO (SAML v2.0) federation with customer IdP
- RBAC role mapping coverage for operator and customer admin personas
- KMS/HSM custody, rotation, and escrow procedures to support audits
- Audit log schema, retention, integrity checks, and forensic export procedures
- Operator runbook items that minimally require privileged action and an approval trail
out_of_scope:
- Internal hosted API pricing changes
- Dedicated capacity autoscaling policies
- Non-crypto operational runbooks unrelated to key management
acceptance_criteria: SAML: Metadata exchange validated; assertion signing algorithm matches customer policy (RSA-SHA256 or better); assertion replay protections and audience checks explicitly tested in staging

RBAC: Principal-to-role mapping documented and tested for all operator flows (create, rotate, revoke keys; escalate session; emergency access); every operator action maps to a named role and a scope-limited permission set
KMS/HSM: Customer KMS key policy documented; HSM backup/restore and quorum/failover plan validated in an airgapped lab; rotation schedule and automated rotation hooks defined

Audit logs: Immutable ledger or signed log chain enabled for all key operations and operator actions; retention meets customer SLA (minimum 1 year) and export supports a forensics delivery format (WARC/JSONL with signatures)
Key escrow: If escrow is required, escrow protocol recorded, escrow custodians listed, and chain-of-custody artifact generation demonstrated
Evidence: Each acceptance item has an evidence artifact (test script results, STS logs, SAML trace, screenshot of RBAC mappings, HSM runbook play-by-play) attached or linked
Sign-off: Security, Legal (if required), and Customer Success each provide explicit sign-off text entry in the acceptance checklist
signoff_checklist: Security review completed and signed (entry: security@redwood-inference), includes HSM threat model annex
SAML exchange test report uploaded (Confluence link) showing end-to-end assertion flow and replay tests
RBAC matrix reviewed by customer and Redwood IAM; customer-approved mapping file stored in onboarding artifacts
KMS/HSM acceptance run executed in staging: pass/fail logs attached
Audit log chain integrity test passed: signed log root hash verified against on-disk copies and uploaded to secure evidence store
Operator runbook reviewed: commands requiring elevated privileges gated with approval tickets and OTP/2FA checks validated
Escrow/rotation policy attached where applicable and legal sign-off collected
Disaster/failover recovery test documented (time-to-restore, data recovery steps) and meets SLOs
Customer Success confirms onboarding checklist is complete and schedules post-go-live observation window
Final sign-off recorded with timestamps and signer names for Security, Product, Customer Success, and the customer technical lead
decisions: Use SAML v2.0 with signed assertions as default federation mechanism for enterprise private deploys
Require HSM-backed key material for any customer-marked PII/PHI workloads where key custody is mandated
Adopt signed audit log chain (hashchain) instead of relying solely on central logging for forensic integrity
Operator actions must always be recorded in a separate immutable audit stream with a one-to-one mapping to an authorization ticket
risks: Delayed customer IdP metadata or non-conformant SAML implementations leading to onboarding delays
HSM vendor-specific limitations that prevent automated rotation workflows—may require manual steps under controlled procedures
Operator error during key rotation could cause temporary service disruption if rollback runbooks are incomplete
Large audit retention windows increase storage and export cost for both Redwood and the customer
